intro: Over 170 nationalities are Indian e-Visa eligible countries. Type yours below to check, or browse the full list. Some people can’t use the e-Visa whatever their nationality, so read the exceptions too.
cardText: Check whether your nationality can apply for an Indian e-Visa.

sections.heading: Who can’t use an e-Visa, whatever their nationality
sections.text:
- People of Pakistani origin, including British citizens whose parents or grandparents were born in or lived permanently in Pakistan. [Read our guide](/indian-visa-for-pakistani-origin/)
- Pakistani passport holders
- Anyone with a military, police, intelligence or security background, serving or retired
- Holders of diplomatic or official passports, and international travel documents other than a passport
- Children listed on a parent’s passport: each person needs their own passport

sections.heading: Other conditions for Indian e-Visa eligible countries
sections.text: Your passport must be valid for at least six months when you apply and have at least two blank pages. You need a return or onward ticket and enough money for your stay. The e-Visa isn’t valid for protected or restricted areas.

sections.heading: Living in the UK on another passport?
sections.text: You can apply from the UK on any eligible passport. You may be asked for proof of your UK residence, such as your eVisa share code or BRP.

sections.heading: What if my country isn’t eligible?
sections.text: If your nationality isn’t on the list of Indian e-Visa eligible countries, you’ll need a regular visa. The process takes longer and your passport goes to the visa application centre, but we handle the form and documents for you.

faqs.q: Can British citizens get an Indian e-Visa?
faqs.a: Yes, unless they are of Pakistani origin or have a military or police background.

faqs.q: My nationality isn’t on the list. What can I do?
faqs.a: You’ll need a regular visa. We can help you apply.
Occasionally. We check it against the official Government of India list and update this page when it changes.
